title: Event sampling taxonomy & retention economics — PRD sketch
body:
Purpose

This doc sketches a taxonomy for sampling customer-managed network and approval events, plus a retention/economics model for audit artefacts in Private deployments. Aim: let operator teams opt into lightweight evidence collection that preserves forensics usefulness while bounding storage and egress cost. This is a draft PRD (product sketch) to align product, SRE, and compliance on pragmatic defaults and knobs.

Context & problem

Private customers want accountability for network/approval actions (VPC handshakes, operator-initiated changes, delegated approvals) but many are cost sensitive: full-fidelity event logs + payloads for every change (pcap-like snapshots, config diffs, signed manifests) is expensive at scale. Conversely, overly aggressive sampling or compaction undermines forensic value and compliance certifications. We need a repeatable, configurable approach that:
- Produces small, queryable evidence bundles for common audit queries
- Escales to full-fidelity capture under high-risk triggers (incidents, policy violations)
- Exposes easy-to-understand knobs to customers and operators for retention and cost/scope tradeoffs

Goals

1) Define an event taxonomy and sampling strategies that map to evidence needs (investigation, compliance spot checks, RCA).
2) Propose a retention-tier model (hot/nearline/archive) with cost math and defaults for Private deployments.
3) Provide operator UX and API primitives for: sampling presets, incident-triggered escalation, and evidence export.
4) Include simple heuristics for minimizing PII and customer-sensitive payloads while preserving provenance.

Non-goals

- This sketch does not finalize cryptographic attestation formats (we assume existing attestation primitives used elsewhere).
- Not prescribing exact compression algorithms; leave to infra/OPS to select in prototype.

Event taxonomy (conceptual)

Level A: Control-plane metadata (always-on, tiny)
- examples: change record id, timestamp, actor id, operation type, route/model reference, result code.
- size: ~50–300 bytes/event.
- value: audit trails, counts, author attribution.
- retention: default hot 90 days; searchable in Console.

Level B: Compact evidence snapshot (sampled)
- examples: base64-encoded config diff summary, 1–3-line CLI output, trimmed stack traces, truncated TLS handshakes, compacted route manifests.
- size: ~2–30KB/event.
- sampling: configurable sampling rate (1%, 10%, 100%) + targeted anchors (see below).
- retention: nearline 180 days default.

Level C: Full-fidelity payload (on-demand/triggered)
- examples: complete syslog tail for change window, full config bundle, pcap snippet of connection, signed operator blob.
- size: variable (10KB–10s MB).
- retention: archive/backed-up (30–365 days depending on SLA/pricing).

Sampling strategies (pluggable primitives)

1) Uniform sampling: every Nth event or fixed percentage. Good for long-term trends and spot checks.
2) Stratified sampling: apply different rates by event class (e.g., network-change events sampled at 20%, config-edit at 5%).
3) Anchor-based sampling: automatically keep Level B/C artifacts for events tied to anchors (customer-defined critical resources, e.g., production VPC IDs, high-privilege operators).
4) Triggered escalation: upon detecting anomaly signals (failed approval counts spikes, unauthorized IPs, cross-account changes), automatically capture the next K events at Level C.
5) Time-windowed capture: when a manual or automated investigation is opened, backfill surrounding events within a configured window (e.g., 10 minutes before to 2 hours after).

Evidence compaction & PII minimization rules (defaults)

- Truncate long strings (default 1KB) and expose a knob for maximum field size.
- Hash sensitive identifiers (use salted HMAC with customer-provided key when required) for analytics while masking raw values.
- Redact payload sections that match customer-configured patterns (e.g., secrets files, API keys).
- Keep provenance headers (actor ID, change id, timestamp, signature) intact to preserve chain-of-custody.

Retention tier model and economics (example default)

- Hot (Searchable): Level A logs + recent Level B samples. Default: 90 days. Cost: baseline low per GB.
- Nearline (Cold queryable): Larger Level B snapshots. Default: 180 days. Cost: ~40–60% of hot storage.
- Archive (Deep storage): Level C full-fidelity captures stored on customer-controlled object storage (recommended) or Redwood-managed archive. Default: 365 days for paid SLAs. Cost: lowest per GB but retrieval latency and egress cost apply.

Quick back-of-envelope: a medium enterprise customer with 50k change events/month, Level A only is ~1 GB/month; if 10% sampled at Level B average 10KB, adds ~50MB/month; occasional Level C snapshots (5 per month at 50MB) adds 250MB. Bound: expect <5GB/month unless customer opts into verbose capture. Provide a cost calculator in Console.

Operator UX & API primitives

Console controls:
- Sampling presets: conservative (1%), standard (5%), forensics (25%), full-capture (100%). Each preset shows estimated monthly cost delta.
- Anchors manager: list of resource ids and operator groups that force higher sampling.
- Incident mode toggle: one-click escalate — captures Level C for next X hours and pins retention.
- Export & escrow: button to push selected evidence bundles to customer S3/GCS with signed manifest.

APIs:
- GET /evidence/events?event_id=..., GET /evidence/bundle/{id} (returns signed bundle metadata + link).
- POST /evidence/escrow -> triggers copy to external store + signed receipt.
- PUT /sampling/policy -> update sampling rules programmatically.

Security & compliance considerations

- Evidence bundles are signed by Redwood private key and optionally re-signed by customer KMS for non-repudiation.
- Access controls: RBAC for who can toggle incident mode or export bundles. Provide audit trail for those actions.
- Data residency: default to customer region; retention rules apply per-region.

Rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA)

MVP (quarter 1):
- Implement Level A logs + basic Level B compact snapshots; uniform & stratified sampling; Console presets and cost estimates.
- Minimal incident toggle that marks events for elevated retention (no automatic Level C capture yet).

Beta (quarter 2):
- Anchors, triggered escalation heuristics, time-window backfill, S3/GCS escrow export.
- Add hash-based PII masking and provenance signing.

GA (quarter 3+):
- Full Level C capture workflows, customer-controlled KMS signing, deeper retention tiering, SLA pricing.

Open questions & trade-offs

- What exact storage/compression stack will infra pick (object store vs append-only DB)? Affects retrieval latency and cost model.
- How to define reasonable defaults for sensitive-data redaction without breaking useful forensics? Need compliance input per-jurisdiction.
- Escalation detection: should Redwood propose default anomaly detectors or leave solely to customers?

Next steps (owners)

- Product: finalize sampling presets and pricing bands (Asha) — due 2025-02-14.
- Infra/SRE: prototype storage prototype and retrieval latency targets (Marco) — due 2025-02-28.
- Security/Privacy: draft redaction patterns and KMS integration plan (Elena) — due 2025-02-21.
- Solutions Eng: identify 3 pilot customers and run capture cost experiments (Samir) — outreach by 2025-02-10.

Notes & references

- This approaches evidence minimization and cost-conscious capture rather than the large-volume immutable ledger used in some private-deploy PRDs. It complements attestation/approval artifacts and should be wired into the rollout/handshake flows already sketched in other docs.
- See linked artifacts at top for early experiments and hypothesis tests.

:end of sketch.
